papers.title: Deterministic and programmable generation of mechanical multipartite entangled states
papers.abstract: Multimode mechanical resonators offer a large set of densely packed, long-lived bosonic modes within a single compact device, making them attractive for quantum simulation, quantum information processing, and quantum-enhanced sensing. Many such applications rely on multipartite entanglement, yet deterministic mechanical entanglement has so far been largely limited to pairs of modes. Here we demonstrate the deterministic and programmable preparation of multipartite entangled states among the phonon modes of a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator coupled to a superconducting transmon qubit. By sequentially applying optimal-control-engineered isometries between the qubit and successive modes, we generate matrix product states of bond dimension two, including $W$, Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ), and cluster states. We fully characterize these states via quantum state tomography and certify genuine multipartite entanglement among up to four modes. We further demonstrate correlated-noise sensing by exploiting the complementary decoherence responses of the stored $W$ and GHZ states, isolating inter-mode phase correlations from local decoherence and placing quantitative bounds on collective dephasing. Our results establish a scalable approach to preparing multipartite entangled states in mechanical systems, with promising applications in multiparameter sensing and tests of quantum mechanics with massive objects.
papers.finding: Using optimal-control-engineered isometries between a transmon qubit and phonon modes of a bulk acoustic wave resonator, the study deterministically prepares matrix product states and certifies genuine multipartite entanglement among up to four mechanical modes.

papers.title: Visualizing Chiral Edge Modes in Twisted Cuprate Superconductors via Scanning-Probe Quantum Sensing
papers.abstract: Recently, unconventional superconductivity hosted by twisted van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures has received immense interest due to the exotic pairing symmetry, electronic interactions and nontrivial topological nature that are naturally relevant to the fast-advancing quantum technologies. Here, we report scanning-probe quantum sensing of nanoscale electromagnetic behaviors of twisted vdW cuprate superconductors. Using single-spin relaxometry, we directly visualize edge modes spontaneously formed in twisted Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x (BSCCO). By investigating temperature dependent variations of edge-state-induced quantum spin relaxation, we experimentally evaluate the magnitude of nontrivial topological band gap opened at nodal points in twisted BSCCO and its critical temperature behaviors under different twist angles. We further observe alternating chiral domains defined by edge modes, exploring experimental signatures of in-plane magnetic field-induced topology in 45° twisted BSCCO. Our results advance the current understanding of twisted vdW nodal superconductors, presenting an appealing high-temperature topological superconducting material platform for cutting-edge quantum innovation.
papers.finding: Using single-spin relaxometry, the study visualizes spontaneously formed edge modes in twisted Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x and evaluates the nontrivial topological band gap and its critical temperature behavior under different twist angles.

papers.title: Field-angle-resolved heat transport in UTe$_2$: determination of nodal positions in the superconducting order parameter
papers.abstract: One of the recurring hurdles in studying unconventional superconductivity is the challenge of efficiently and conclusively identifying the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter in a new material. Uranium ditelluride (UTe$_2$) exhibits an unprecedented number of superconducting phases as a function of pressure and magnetic field, each presumably characterized by a different symmetry of the superconducting gap function. None of these phases has had its symmetry conclusively identified so far. In this article, we report results of an extensive study of the thermal conductivity of UTe$_2$ in its low-field, low-temperature superconducting state as a function of the angle of an applied magnetic field rotated in the $b$-$c$ plane. We observe clear and substantial oscillations in the thermal conductivity as a function of field angle, which naturally suggests the existence of point nodes in the gap. Utilizing the experimentally determined Fermi surface, we are able to model this phenomenon for all the potential gap structures in UTe$_2$ and positively identify the location of these nodes as being along the crystallographic $b$-axis, implying that the superconducting order parameter belongs to the $B_{2u}$ irreducible representation of the crystal point group. The clarity of this result will accelerate the identification of other superconducting phases in UTe$_2$, and guide future studies through the use of high resolution field-angle-dependent measurements.
papers.finding: Using field-angle-dependent thermal conductivity measurements and modeling with the experimentally determined Fermi surface, the study identifies point nodes along the crystallographic b-axis, implying a B2u superconducting order parameter in UTe2.

papers.title: The role of dependency range in thermally coupled superconducting networks
papers.abstract: Interdependent networks can be highly fragile because dependency links amplify local failures into cascades that trigger global collapse. Much of the theoretical understanding comes from geometric network models, where dependency range is imposed externally and coupling strength is distance independent, and it is unclear how these insights apply to real materials, where interdependence arises from physical transport. Here we study thermally coupled amorphous superconducting networks, in which dependencies emerge from current redistribution and heat-mediated interactions governed by thermal diffusivity. Using an experimentally calibrated model of resistively shunted Josephson junctions, we show the system reproduces the three canonical transition regimes: continuous, nucleation-dominated, and mixed-order. However, because heat-driven dependency simultaneously broadens and weakens with distance, long-range thermal coupling can stabilize the superconducting phase upon heating, in contrast with its destabilizing role in geometric models. Cascades are anisotropic, with one-dimensional front propagation. These results offer an experimentally testable perspective complementing the geometric framework.
papers.finding: Using an experimentally calibrated model of resistively shunted Josephson junctions for thermally coupled amorphous superconducting networks, the study finds that long-range thermal coupling can stabilize the superconducting phase upon heating, with anisotropic cascades.

papers.title: Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity near Phase Boundaries in Rhombohedral Multilayer Graphene
papers.abstract: The recent observation of superconductivity in untwisted multilayer graphene has sparked intense interest in its microscopic origin. As the displacement field and carrier density are varied, superconductivity emerges in several distinct regions with different temperature and magnetic-field responses. This behavior has been attributed to the presence of distinct electronic phases, raising the possibility that different superconducting regions originate from different microscopic mechanisms. While purely electronic pairing mechanisms have been extensively explored, an in-depth examination of phonon-mediated superconductivity is still missing. Here, we solve the coupled selfconsistent Migdal-Eliashberg equations using input from first-principles calculations and incorporating interaction-driven symmetry breaking of the electronic ground state. Varying the carrier density and displacement field, we reproduce the experimentally observed superconducting regions with comparable superconducting properties such as gap and $T_c$ and predict additional, as-yet undiscovered superconducting phases. Our findings exemplify that several superconductivity regions in rhombohedral graphene can be satisfactorily explained by phonon-mediated pairing.
papers.finding: Using coupled self-consistent Migdal-Eliashberg equations with first-principles input and interaction-driven symmetry breaking, the study reproduces the experimentally observed superconducting regions in rhombohedral graphene via phonon-mediated pairing.

papers.title: Imaging how fluctuations destroy superconductivity in two dimensions
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional superconductors test our understanding of quantum phases. Low-temperature "anomalous metal" states are widely observed where conventional theories predict only superconducting or insulating ground states. In model systems based on proximity-coupled Josephson junction arrays, the critical temperature falls far faster with decreasing normal-state conductance than predicted by existing models. Whether these observations indicate a new quantum phase, a need to refine models of disorder and fluctuations, or both remains unresolved. Using scanning magnetic susceptometry, we image the local superfluid phase stiffness $ρ_s$ in gate-tunable Josephson junction arrays consisting of epitaxial Al islands on an InAs quantum well. Across six arrays and more than two orders of magnitude in the zero-temperature phase stiffness $ρ_{s0}$, the diamagnetic critical temperature $T_{c,\varphi}$ is suppressed more strongly than can be explained solely by thermal phase fluctuations, scaling approximately as $T_{c,\varphi}\proptoρ_{s0}^{0.3}$. While $ρ_s$ is remarkably uniform at high carrier densities, at low carrier densities we find that anomalous metal transport emerges together with large-scale inhomogeneity that transport alone cannot directly detect. These results are inconsistent with a classical XY description within standard junction models, instead pointing to quantum fluctuations that suppress superconductivity throughout the superconducting phase and amplify inhomogeneity near the superconductor-insulator transition, producing anomalous metal behavior.
papers.finding: Using scanning magnetic susceptometry on gate-tunable Josephson junction arrays, the study finds the diamagnetic critical temperature scales as Tc ∝ ρs0^0.3, with anomalous metal transport emerging alongside large-scale inhomogeneity at low carrier densities.

papers.title: Quantitative Impact of Occupation Smearing Methods on Conventional Superconductivity: from Electronic Structure through Lattice Dynamics to Electron-Phonon Coupling
papers.abstract: In first-principles calculations of metallic systems, the discrete electronic mesh in the Brillouin zone necessitates a smearing function and its width (e.g., the widely used 0.02 Ry Methfessel-Paxton scheme) to enforce continuity of energy and occupation at the Fermi surface. However, the quantitative impact of such empirical parameters on phonon-mediated superconductivity has long been overlooked, leading to their habitual selection by mere convention. Here, using hexahydride CsH6 as a benchmark, we systematically investigate the magnitude and propagation mechanism of smearing-induced errors against the parameter-free optimized tetrahedron method. Long-tailed smearing delocalizes the occupation window, causing substantial Fermi-level shifts, flattening of the density of states, and hardening phonon modes, thereby weakening electron-phonon coupling. Conversely, short-tailed smearing suffers from insufficient sampling, producing density-of-states oscillations and enhanced Fermi-surface nesting; via amplified electronic screening and Peierls instabilities, this softens acoustic modes and generates imaginary frequencies, causing CsH6 to be dynamically unstable and discarded. However, the optimized tetrahedron method reveals that CsH6 is dynamically stable under ambient pressure with a remarkable superconducting transition temperature of 121 K. To prevent subjective empirical parameters from obscuring theoretically promising high-temperature superconductors, we derive a simple scaling relation for the smearing width, applicable to different smearing functions, from the free-electron-gas model, offering an objective, precise, and efficient protocol for parameter selection in high-throughput screening.
papers.finding: Using first-principles calculations benchmarked on CsH6 against the optimized tetrahedron method, the study finds smearing-induced errors weaken electron-phonon coupling, while the parameter-free method gives a stable CsH6 with a superconducting transition temperature of 121 K.

papers.title: Effects of the choice of the exchange-correlation functional on high-temperature superconductivity predictions in covalent-cage M(BN)5 family
papers.abstract: The recent experimental synthesis of covalent cage superconductors has ignited hopes for ambient-pressure high-temperature superconductivity, while the computational strategy for discovering new materials poses challenges for accurately estimating superconducting properties. Here, we quantified the response of electron-phonon coupling (EPC) properties in M(BN)5 superconductors to different exchange-correlation (XC) effects using high-throughput first-principles calculations. We found that the metallic covalent bonds responsible for superconductivity exhibit anomalously high sensitivity to functional selection uncertainty, distinguishing them from conventional superconductors mediated by metallic bonding. The widely used PBE functional systematically overestimates lattice volumes, inducing phonon softening, enhanced EPC, and consequent Peierls instability. In contrast, PBEsol, which is more accurate through enhanced treatment of short-range interactions, eliminates imaginary frequencies in Rb(BN)5 that appear at the PBE level, yielding an outstanding superconducting critical temperature (Tc) of 113 K at ambient pressure and 138 K at 2 GPa. Enhanced electron localization and short-range correlation in covalent bonds manifest through dual mechanisms: phonon hardening at the lattice scale and band widening at the electronic scale, which collectively suppress Peierls distortion and delocalize antibonding states. Pressure-dependent analysis reveals that compression attenuates phonon discrepancies between XC functionals, whereas electronic properties remain notably sensitive to XC-induced perturbations of fine electronic bands near the Fermi level.
papers.finding: Using high-throughput first-principles calculations on M(BN)5 superconductors, the study finds exchange-correlation functional choice strongly affects electron-phonon coupling, with PBEsol yielding a Tc of 113 K at ambient pressure for Rb(BN)5.

papers.title: Local error correction prolongs time-crystalline memory
papers.abstract: Discrete time crystals are non-equilibrium phases of matter with spatiotemporal order and a response that breaks the time-translation symmetry of a periodic external drive. Interactions, spatial disorder and correlated random driving can in theory stabilize this order. In experiments, however, coupling to the environment limits the time crystal lifetime. Here we use stochastic local bit-flip error correction to prolong the time-crystalline response of a driven, spatially disordered two-dimensional Ising model on a superconducting quantum processor, using a repetition code with distances three and five on a honeycomb lattice with up to 68 physical qubits. Even though ancilla qubits, midcircuit syndrome measurements and decoding increase the required quantum and classical resources, the stochastic drive increases the memory decay time by a factor of up to two. At late times we observe that recovery stabilizes spatial order across the lattice. The spin-configuration distributions explain this separation, as recovery suppresses disagreeing bonds while broadening occupies completely reversed states. Syndrome measurements without correction accelerate the memory decay, demonstrating the importance of conditional correction. Our results show that local bit-flip error correction can preserve time-crystalline memory over more drive cycles than the bare dynamics.
papers.finding: Using stochastic local bit-flip error correction on up to 68 qubits of a superconducting processor, the study finds the time-crystalline memory decay time increases by up to a factor of two.

papers.title: Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Is Fermionic Magic
papers.abstract: Free fermion dynamics is classically simulable, and a single non-Gaussian state makes it universal. We show that the same boundary governs quantum nonlocality. Measured as fermionic qubits, fermionic Gaussian states reach at most the biseparable bound of the Mermin inequality for three parties and, for any number of parties, violate the Mermin family by exactly the factor of a single entangled pair. They are never genuinely multipartite nonlocal. Genuine multipartite nonlocality and computational universality are thus one resource for fermions, the opposite of the stabilizer case. The mechanism is fermion parity. The bound is monogamous and certifies non-Gaussianity from measured correlations alone. On superconducting processors we watch nonlocality beyond free fermions switch on under an interaction between densities, confirm the monogamy law on 96 qubits, and measure the ground state of twelve interacting fermions on a ring cross the bound as the interaction grows, detecting the charge density wave transition.
papers.finding: Using superconducting processors and the Mermin inequality, the study finds fermionic Gaussian states are never genuinely multipartite nonlocal, with the bound confirmed on 96 qubits and crossed by twelve interacting fermions on a ring.

papers.title: Weyl superconductivity from Feshbach resonance in the three-dimensional repulsive Hubbard model
papers.abstract: Motivated by the first experimental realization of the antiferromagnetic phase transition in the three-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model, we present a theoretical study of the model's 3D superconducting phase. By formulating a 3D extension of the Feshbach mechanism, we provide a unified microscopic picture at strong coupling in which pairing is driven by near-resonant bound states of dopants. These long-lived bound states acquire a qualitatively different internal structure in three dimensions compared to their two-dimensional counterparts, giving rise to a distinct superconducting state, namely a time-reversal symmetry breaking $d_{x^2-y^2}+id_{z^2}$ pairing state. We also provide an estimate of the corresponding critical temperature, and provide evidence that the resulting superconducting phase hosts gapless Weyl points. Our results represent a new milestone for the field of quantum simulation, challenging experiments and large-scale numerics alike to test our predictions.
papers.finding: Using a 3D extension of the Feshbach mechanism, the study finds that strong-coupling pairing via near-resonant dopant bound states yields a time-reversal symmetry breaking d_{x²−y²}+id_{z²} superconducting state.
